actors.name: Taliban / Islamic Emirate Security Apparatus
actors.summary: De facto governing security system established by the Taliban after its August 2021 takeover. Public reporting and Taliban official material show a centralized leadership structure spanning the Ministry of National Defense, Ministry of Interior and General Directorate of Intelligence. The United States has not recognized the Taliban as the government of Afghanistan.

sources.label: UN Secretary-General report on Afghanistan, S/2025/372
U.S. State Department — Country Reports on Terrorism: Afghanistan
CIA World Factbook — Afghanistan

leadership.name: Haibatullah Akhundzada
leadership.note: UN reporting describes central authority over de facto security officials.

structure: De facto Cabinet and senior security officials

actors.name: Ministry of National Defense — Islamic Emirate
actors.summary: De facto defense ministry directing the Taliban-era national military. Current official ministry material identifies regional army corps, a central corps, an air force and special-forces structures; exact manning and readiness are not consistently published.

actors.name: Ministry of Interior Affairs — Islamic Emirate
actors.summary: De facto interior ministry responsible for policing and internal-security functions. Its current public structure includes security operations, border police, counter-crime, police special units, traffic and Interpol functions, with counter-narcotics institutions also active.

leadership.name: Sirajuddin Haqqani
leadership.note: Also a senior Haqqani Network figure; HQN remains a U.S.-designated FTO.

actors.name: General Directorate of Intelligence (GDI)
actors.summary: De facto national intelligence and internal-security service. UN reporting identifies Abdul Haq Wasiq as the head of the GDI and describes the directorate as part of the Taliban security apparatus, including activity against ISIS-K and internal security targets.

actors.name: Afghan Air Force / Air Force General Command
actors.summary: Air component under the de facto Ministry of National Defense. Taliban official reporting has shown efforts to restore inherited aircraft and helicopters; fleet availability is fluid and published inventory totals should not be treated as serviceable-aircraft counts.

systems.name: Mi-17
systems.note: Official reporting confirms continuing operation; serviceable quantity changes.

systems.name: MD-530 family
systems.note: Taliban MoD has publicly displayed aircraft from this family.

systems.name: Cessna C-208
systems.note: Inherited platform; current mission availability varies.

systems.name: Mi-35
systems.note: Publicly displayed by Taliban MoD; serviceability varies.

actors.name: MoD General Command of Special Forces
actors.summary: Special-operations organization under the de facto Ministry of National Defense. Official MoD reporting confirms a general command for special forces, while subordinate organization and current readiness are only partially visible in open sources.

actors.name: General Directorate of Border Police
actors.summary: Border-security organization under the Ministry of Interior. Current ministry reporting identifies a Director General, military and logistics deputies, subordinate border-crossing personnel and continuing capacity-building activity.

actors.name: General Command of Police Special Units
actors.summary: Police special-operations structure under the Ministry of Interior's security chain. Official ministry pages list a General Command of Police Special Units and report national/provincial special-force training.

sources.label: Afghanistan MoI — Deputy Ministry of Security
Afghanistan MoI — Police Special Forces

actors.name: Afghanistan — Key Military Airfields & Garrison Hubs
actors.summary: Reference node for major inherited military facilities and garrison centers used by Afghan security forces. Kabul-area military facilities, Kandahar, Shindand, Mazar-e Sharif, Jalalabad and Bagram remain important reference points, but current tenant units and operational intensity should be verified against recent reporting before use.
